description: methodology 1.7 — the one-sided slope barrier: the fit with it at weight 0.3 against the barrier removed and the barrier at ten times that weight. MEASURED WITH THE BARRIER AS ITS REFERENCE: the arms named `shipped` ran weight 0.3, which is what a config of {} meant when they were recorded; production has since moved to NO barrier (`barrier_off`'s configuration) on this panel's evidence. Re-running the panel needs the reference arms to declare `shallow_w` 0.3 explicitly, since {} now runs without it. The questions: how far the derived ratings blow out without the barrier (the 99.9th percentile runs to over a hundred units, one-sided, about the same at every seed) and what that costs held-out (nothing — marginally better at every seed); and whether ten times the weight compresses the range or costs likelihood (narrower at two seeds of three, no resolved cost). EVERY ARM RUNS AT THREE SEEDS: within one seed the arms hold aside the same stop rows and the delta is paired, and the seeds are independent paired estimates whose agreement in SIGN is what the producer quotes a contrast on.
